S.TRANSL: An eel came to block the water of the river sideways.
It blocked the river to increase the water level.
People escaped to a small mountain.
The water came to submerge it.

S.FORM: mu-caanə cau ala-vali mu-kusa tinumulumulu nausərana.
S.PHON: muʦaanə ʦau aɾavaɾi mukusa tinumuɾumuɾu nausərana
S.FORM: mucaane cau aravari mukusa tinumurumuru nauserana.
S.PHON: muʦaane ʦau a[r|ɾ]ava[r|ɾ]i mukusa tinumu[r|ɾ]umu[r|ɾ]u nause[r|ɾ]ana
S.TRANSL: People left it and moved to Mountain Nauserana.
They lived there.
They stayed there together with wild animals.
They could not eat without a fire.
They discussed that they would hire someone to go and get a fire at this difficult time.

S.FORM: ʔini-maamia taʔuruŋu tavalaʔə maka-naŋulu mu-caanə mu-kusa tanuʔuŋʔincu, ʔuuna apulu.
S.PHON: ʔinimaamia taʔuruŋu tavaɾaʔə makanaŋuɾu muʦaanə mukusa tanuʔuŋʔinʦu ʔuuna apuɾu
S.FORM: 'inimaamia ta'urungu tavara'e makananguru mucaane mukusa tanu'ung'incu, 'uuna apuru.
S.PHON: ʔinimaamia taʔu[r|ɾ]uŋu tava[r|ɾ]aʔe makanaŋu[r|ɾ]u muʦaane mukusa tanuʔuŋʔinʦu ʔuuna apu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: Only a muntjac could swim to Mount Tanu'ung'incu, where there was fire.

S.FORM: pu-aiʔi taʔuruŋu um-a-avici apulu, i-vatu tinmulumulu nausərana.
S.PHON: puaiʔi taʔuruŋu umaavitʂi apuɾu ivatu tinmuɾumuɾu nausərana
S.FORM: puai'i ta'urungu umaavici apuru, ivatu tinmurumuru nauserana.
S.PHON: puaiʔi taʔu[r|ɾ]uŋu umaavitʂi apu[r|ɾ]u ivatu tinmu[r|ɾ]umu[r|ɾ]u nause[r|ɾ]ana
S.TRANSL: The muntjac returned with a fire to Mount Nauserana.
People were very happy.
They cooked food since then.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia ma-kari-kari cau mata mara-kəra-kərapə.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia makarikari ʦau mata marakərakərapə
a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia maka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i ʦau mata ma[r|ɾ]ake[r|ɾ]ake[r|ɾ]ape
S.TRANSL: People talked with wild animals since then.

S.FORM: m-ali-vali vavulu, "mu-a-caa=ku=ʔai mu-kusa ʔinia m-ia-pacai vərəŋa."
S.PHON: maɾivaɾi vavuɾu muaʦaakuʔai mukusa ʔinia miapaʦai vərəŋa
ma[r|ɾ]iva[r|ɾ]i vavu[r|ɾ]u muaʦaakuʔai mukusa ʔinia miapaʦai ve[r|ɾ]eŋa
S.TRANSL: The wild pig replied, "I shall go and kill the eel."

S.FORM: pu-kari-kari vavulu, "a-pa-kaən-a=ʔai ma-manu=maku ni-əməkə=mu si tia=ku mu-a-kusa ʔinia m-aku-tərəkə vərəŋa."
S.PHON: pukarikari vavuɾu apakaənaʔai mamanumaku niəməkəmu ʂi tiaku muakusa ʔinia makutərəkə vərəŋa
S.FORM: pukarikari vavuru, "apakaena'ai mamanumaku niemekemu si tiaku muakusa 'inia makutereke verenga."
S.PHON: puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i vavu[r|ɾ]u apakaenaʔai mamanumaku niemekemu ʂi tiaku muakusa ʔinia makute[r|ɾ]eke ve[r|ɾ]eŋa
S.TRANSL: The wild pig said, "You will have to support my children with what you plant because I'll go and cut the eel apart."
It drifted to where (the eel) was.

S.FORM: m-i-raʔisi=kiai m-aku-tərəkə vərəŋa, ki-papa ʔinia ma-ʔacunu.
S.PHON: miraʔiʂikiai makutərəkə vərəŋa kipapa ʔinia maʔaʦunu
mi[r|ɾ]aʔiʂikiai makute[r|ɾ]eke ve[r|ɾ]eŋa kipapa ʔinia maʔaʦunu
S.TRANSL: It bit the eel and cut it apart, and it drifted down with it.
There was no more water since then.
(The ground) became very uneven (full of bumps and holes) since then.

S.FORM: ʔuuna m-alə-ŋəcai ʔənai si nimi-valu ʔənai.
S.PHON: ʔuuna maɾəŋəʦai ʔənai ʂi nimivaɾu ʔənai
ʔuuna ma[r|ɾ]eŋeʦai ʔenai ʂi nimiva[r|ɾ]u ʔenai
S.TRANSL: There were highlands because of mud.

S.FORM: mia ara-nakarə=cu canumu ia, aranai ʔinia cau maa-vua-vuarə mata mara-kəra-kərapə.
S.PHON: mia aranakarəʦu ʦanumu ia aranai ʔinia ʦau maavuavuarə mata marakərakərapə
S.FORM: mia aranakarecu canumu ia, aranai 'inia cau maavuavuare mata marakerakerape.
S.PHON: mia a[r|ɾ]anaka[r|ɾ]eʦu ʦanumu ia a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia ʦau maavuavua[r|ɾ]e mata ma[r|ɾ]ake[r|ɾ]ake[r|ɾ]ape
S.TRANSL: When the water dried up, people kept themselves away from wild animals ever since.
We (people) discussed, "We're people, while you're wild animals."
The wild animals said, "We can smell your bad smell."
"In spite of that, we'll shoot you," (people said to them).

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia nuu c<um>əʔəra ʔinia m-ia-ʔicəpə=cu, si tia=cu panaʔ-ənə.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia nuu ʦuməʔəra ʔinia miaʔiʦəpəʦu ʂi tiaʦu panaʔənə
S.FORM: aranai 'inia nuu c<um>e'era 'inia mia'icepecu, si tiacu pana'ene.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia nuu ʦumeʔe[r|ɾ]a ʔinia miaʔiʦepeʦu ʂi tiaʦu panaʔene
S.TRANSL: Since that time, they were afraid to see (people) because they would shoot them.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia mu-kusa nacəŋa mu-ʔuna=cu ʔinia ka-ʔuma-ʔuma.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia mukusa naʦəŋa muʔunaʦu ʔinia kaʔumaʔuma
a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia mukusa naʦeŋa muʔunaʦu ʔinia kaʔumaʔuma
S.TRANSL: Since then (people) went to live and cultivate (fields) in Nacenga.
People were happy to have food.

S.FORM: mia-iisua ia, ma-kaŋəcə ʔuma ʔapacuʔ-ai ia, i-tumulu kaən-a.
S.PHON: miaiisua ia makaŋəʦə ʔuma ʔapaʦuʔai ia itumuɾu kaəna
S.FORM: miaiisua ia, makangece 'uma 'apacu'ai ia, itumuru kaena.
S.PHON: miaiisua ia makaŋeʦe ʔuma ʔapaʦuʔai ia itumu[r|ɾ]u kaena
S.TRANSL: Although there were few fields, there was plenty of food.
They could not consume all the food in one year.
At that time, (people) were always very happy.
There was not any disease as yet.
They lived in Nacenga for a long time.

S.FORM: ara-kacaua=pa cau, ma-məməkə=cu ʔakia=cu ta-kamaanəŋ-a ʔuma.
S.PHON: arakaʦauapa ʦau maməməkəʦu ʔakiaʦu takamaanəŋa ʔuma
a[r|ɾ]akaʦauapa ʦau mamemekeʦu ʔakiaʦu takamaaneŋa ʔuma
S.TRANSL: The population increased, and they were worried that there was not enough field to work on.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia ala-vali natanasa, ka-ʔuma-ʔuma ma-kaŋəcə.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia aɾavaɾi natanasa kaʔumaʔuma makaŋəʦə
a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia a[r|ɾ]ava[r|ɾ]i natanasa kaʔumaʔuma makaŋeʦe
S.TRANSL: Since that time, they moved to Natanasa, with a few fields to cultivate.

S.FORM: ki-papa ʔinia tacau-ini ni-pivəra, mu-ʔuna ʔinia ka-manu-manu.
S.PHON: kipapa ʔinia taʦauini nipivəra muʔuna ʔinia kamanumanu
kipapa ʔinia taʦauini nipive[r|ɾ]a muʔuna ʔinia kamanumanu
S.TRANSL: The dog that followed them became pregnant, stayed there and gave birth to puppie.

S.FORM: tia=pa pu-aiʔi nacəŋa si ʔaisi=pa ʔinia kaən-a-ini aʔun-ai ʔinia.
S.PHON: tiapa puaiʔi naʦəŋa ʂi ʔaiʂipa ʔinia kaənaini aʔunai ʔinia
S.FORM: tiapa puai'i nacenga si 'aisipa 'inia kaenaini a'unai 'inia.
S.PHON: tiapa puaiʔi naʦeŋa ʂi ʔaiʂipa ʔinia kaenaini aʔunai ʔinia
S.TRANSL: (People) returned to Nacenga because some food had been left there and they wanted to carry it (on back to the new home).

S.FORM: i-vatu cina tacau l<um>aaŋan manu-ini aiʔi natanasa.
S.PHON: ivatu tʂina taʦau ɾumaaŋan manuini aiʔi natanasa
S.FORM: ivatu cina tacau r<um>aangan manuini ai'i natanasa.
S.PHON: ivatu tʂina taʦau [r|ɾ]umaaŋan manuini aiʔi natanasa
S.TRANSL: A female dog came to take puppies to return to Natanasa.
Dogs followed those who carried food (on their backs).
They lived and built houses there.
All people came to build their houses.
All people lived there for a long time.

S.FORM: ka-ʔuma-ʔuma kaa-vaŋəvaŋə mia-iisua ia, kaʔanə=pa ma-sukuamə cau.
S.PHON: kaʔumaʔuma kaavaŋəvaŋə miaiisua ia kaʔanəpa masukuamə ʦau
S.FORM: ka'uma'uma kaavangevange miaiisua ia, ka'anepa masukuame cau.
S.PHON: kaʔumaʔuma kaavaŋevaŋe miaiisua ia kaʔanepa masukuame ʦau
S.TRANSL: All people cultivated their fields, and people did not get sick yet.
They lived there for a long time, and the population increased.
Since that time, there have been many people.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia aka-cəpəŋ-ini pakisia i-vatu pari-tanasə.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia akaʦəpəŋini pakiʂia ivatu paritanasə
a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia akaʦepeŋini pakiʂia ivatu pa[r|ɾ]itanase
S.TRANSL: Since that time, people suffered because the Chinese came to drive them away.
There was a fight and they killed each other, and the Kanakanavu lost seventy people.
They did not bury the dead.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia um-aŋuru ala-vali ʔəməmələ mia-ranau.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia umaŋuru aɾavaɾi ʔəməməɾə miaranau
a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia umaŋu[r|ɾ]u a[r|ɾ]ava[r|ɾ]i ʔememe[r|ɾ]e mia[r|ɾ]anau
S.TRANSL: Since that time they escaped to 'Ememele and stayed there for a long time.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia mu-kusa tavarana, cucuma-ini ni-mu-kusa ʔaŋʔuana cucuma-ini.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia mukusa tavarana ʦuʦumaini nimukusa ʔaŋʔuana ʦuʦumaini
S.FORM: aranai 'inia mukusa tavarana, cucumaini nimukusa 'ang'uana cucumaini.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia mukusa tava[r|ɾ]ana ʦuʦumaini nimukusa ʔaŋʔuana ʦuʦumaini
S.TRANSL: From then on some people moved to Tavarana, and the others moved to 'Ang'uana.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia tani-uraʔa-i sua pakisia paka-sukuamə, macai ka-vaŋəvaŋə cau. kanaira=cu kau=pa-i macai.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia taniuraʔai sua pakiʂia pakasukuamə maʦai kavaŋəvaŋə ʦau kanairaʦu kaupai maʦai
S.FORM: aranai 'inia taniura'ai sua pakisia pakasukuame, macai kavangevange cau. kanairacu kaupai macai.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia taniu[r|ɾ]aʔai sua pakiʂia pakasukuame maʦai kavaŋevaŋe ʦau kanai[r|ɾ]aʦu kaupai maʦai
S.TRANSL: Since that time the Chinese cursed all Kanakanavu people to be sick. Most people died, and only a few survived.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia ala-vali tanəʔəcə, mu-ʔuna=cu ʔinia ka-ʔuma-ʔuma mia-ranau.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia aɾavaɾi tanəʔəʦə muʔunaʦu ʔinia kaʔumaʔuma miaranau
S.FORM: aranai 'inia aravari tane'ece, mu'unacu 'inia ka'uma'uma miaranau.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia a[r|ɾ]ava[r|ɾ]i taneʔeʦe muʔunaʦu ʔinia kaʔumaʔuma mia[r|ɾ]anau
S.TRANSL: From then on they moved to Tane'ece, lived, and cultivated fields there for a long time.

S.FORM: i-vatu kananavuru. ma-ʔunuŋu cau. ʔakia ni-macai cau, i-tumulu ni-macai kananavuru.
S.PHON: ivatu kananavuru maʔunuŋu ʦau ʔakia nimaʦai ʦau itumuɾu nimaʦai kananavuru
S.FORM: ivatu kananavuru. ma'unungu cau. 'akia nimacai cau, itumuru nimacai kananavuru.
S.PHON: ivatu kananavu[r|ɾ]u maʔunuŋu ʦau ʔakia nimaʦai ʦau itumu[r|ɾ]u nimaʦai kananavu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: (The Chinese) came from Kananavuru. People fought. No (Kanakanavu) died, while many (Chinese people) from Kananavuru died.

S.FORM: aranai mia-sua ʔakia=cu tanasa, ni-namarə kananavuru.
S.PHON: aranai miasua ʔakiaʦu tanasa ninamarə kananavuru
a[r|ɾ]anai miasua ʔakiaʦu tanasa ninama[r|ɾ]e kananavu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: Since that time the Kanakanavu people had no home, burned by the Chinese from Kananavuru.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia mu-kusa naʔəvuana, ka-manəŋə tanasa.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia mukusa naʔəvuana kamanəŋə tanasa
a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia mukusa naʔevuana kamaneŋe tanasa
S.TRANSL: Since that time the Kanakanavu people moved to Na'evuana (an old village) and built houses there.

S.FORM: aranai ʔinia ka-ʔuma-ʔuma mu-a-ʔuna ʔinia mia-ranau.
S.PHON: aranai ʔinia kaʔumaʔuma muaʔuna ʔinia miaranau
a[r|ɾ]anai ʔinia kaʔumaʔuma muaʔuna ʔinia mia[r|ɾ]anau
S.TRANSL: Since that time they cultivated fields, and lived there for a long time.
The fields were very poor.
They moved to Rancurunga from there.
